Championship winning head coach Stuart Gore returns for his third season at Troy.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2024, Gore led the Trojans to a 5-9-3 record, which included a 4-2-1 record in the Trojans' non-conference slate. Troy's offense ranked second in the Sun Belt Conference in corner kicks per game (5.29) while getting an abundance of production from its young core as 47.2% of the team's points came from freshman and sophomores.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nGore was hired by Troy in 2023 with seven years of collegiate head coaching experience, having won 81.3 percent of his games and five conference championships. During his first season at the helm, Gore took over a 3-9-4 Trojan club and doubled their win total going 6-10-2. Troy's defense saw a massive improvement under Gore, holding opponents to 0.50 less goals per game compared to the season prior.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nGore came to Troy following a highly successful two-year stint as the head coach at Northwestern State, where he led the Demons to 25 wins, an NCAA Tournament appearance, two Southland Conference Player of the Year honorees and a No. 61 final RPI ranking in 2022.\u003Cbr />\r\n  \u003Cbr />\r\nUnder Gore's leadership, Northwestern State led the country in corners in 2022 and ranked in the top 25 percent nationally in all attacking and defending categories. The Demons finished the 2022 season with a 12-4-3 overall record. Additionally, Gore added Gracie Armstrong to the program as a graduate transfer, and she would go on to earn Southland Conference Player of the Year honors after scoring 26 points with nine goals and eight assists.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nArmstrong's honor was the second in as many years for Gore and the Demons after Olivia Draguicevich was named the SLC Player of the Year in 2021. Northwestern State won the SLC regular season and tournament championships to advance to the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2005. The regular season championship was the program's first since 2000 and earned Gore SLC Coach of the Year honors.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nThe Demons' goalkeeper Acelya Aydogmus posted 12 shutouts during the championship season, the second-most in the country, while Draguicevich's seven game-winning goals also ranked second nationally.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nBetween his tenures as head coach at Northwestern State and Northwestern Ohio, Gore served as the associate head coach at North Dakota (2020) and James Madison (2018-19).\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nGore built the Northwestern Ohio program from the ground up, leading the Racers to an NAIA National Championships, four straight NAIA Final Four appearances, a 100-15-5 overall record, a national player of the year and 23 All-Americans.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nHe had immediate success in the program's inaugural season, leading Northwestern Ohio to a 15-5-1 record, springboarding the program to four straight 20-win seasons before he moved on to James Madison.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nIt took just three seasons for Gore to lead the Racers to the NAIA National Championship Game and 16 shutouts (most in the country) and then in Gore's fourth season, he brought a National Championship to the program. The 2016 squad led the country with 20 shutouts, boasting the National Player of the Year and five All-Americans.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nPrior to Northwestern Ohio, Gore accumulated coaching experience at every level of soccer. Before joining the Racers, he was the head coach for the Philadelphia Fever of the WPSL (2011-12) and the Director of Coaching at Washington United Soccer Club (2009-12).\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nAs a player, Gore represented England at nearly every youth level, playing for his country's U14 through U18 teams from 1993-2001, in addition to competing with Leeds United from 1996-2000.
